title: Keep AWS Agent Registry fresh with push-based sync
caption:
You deploy a new tool on your MCP server on Monday. Does your agent registry know on Tuesday?

AWS published a push-based way to keep AWS Agent Registry records fresh, so consumers stop reading stale tool schemas.

The flow:
CloudTrail sees UpdateAgentRuntime, EventBridge routes it, a Lambda calls tools/list on the server, diffs it against the record, and updates the record only if something changed.

The part I like: the update drops the record back to Draft until a curator approves it, so automation cannot skip review.

Know the limits before you copy it: it only updates records that are already APPROVED, and CloudTrail delivery takes about 5 to 15 minutes.

Save this if you run MCP servers at scale. Does your team review catalog changes today? Tell me in the comments.

Source: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/automating-aws-agent-registry-updates-with-push-based-architecture/

slides.headline: Your MCP server changed. Your registry is ==still stale.==
slides.sub: A push-based sync pattern from AWS, step by step.

slides.title: Why stale records hurt
paragraphs: A tool gets added or its schema changes, but the registry record does not.
Consumers **miss the new tool**, or call it with an **outdated schema** and get silent workflow deviations.
slides.callout: A catalog is only useful while it is fresh.

slides.title: The sync in five steps
slides.foot: Works in ==one account or across two.==

slides.title: The trigger rule
slides.foot: Fires on every ==UpdateAgentRuntime== in the account.

slides.title: The Lambda does a quiet diff
paragraphs: It sorts tools by name and compares **name, description and inputSchema**.
Same result means **no write**. Different means it logs what was added or removed, then updates the record.
Auth goes through **AgentCore Identity**, so no client secrets sit in the Lambda.

slides.title: Automation cannot skip review
paragraphs: When the Lambda updates a record, it **reverts to Draft**.
Consumers keep seeing the **last approved version** until a curator or administrator approves the update.

cards.title: Cold server
cards.fix: AWS suggests backoff, and skipping when the count is zero.

slides.title: What you set up first
paragraphs: A registry record must **already exist** for the server.
Its server schema must embed the **runtime ARN**. That is how the Lambda matches a CloudTrail event to a record.
slides.callout: Then approve the record so the sync can find it.
